title: Selfie Proportions Look Different? Check Camera Distance
description: See why close camera distance changes selfie perspective. Test viewpoint and screen fill light separately before judging the saved photo.
direct: If a close selfie makes your features look different, move the phone farther away and reframe. Keep your head angle and light steady so you can compare the distance.
figureAlt: Simulated matched portraits illustrate how changing camera distance can change perspective.
figureCaption: AI-generated camera-distance simulation, not a face correction, optical test or GlowPop export.
cards.decision.heading: Start with the decision
cards.decision.body: Perspective depends on the camera’s position relative to the subject. At close range, features nearer the lens occupy more of the picture relative to features farther back. Lighting changes visibility and shadows; it does not move the camera viewpoint.
sections.detail-0.heading: Distance creates a lighting tradeoff
sections.detail-0.body: Moving the phone farther away changes the viewpoint and usually reduces how much its screen illuminates the face. Add suitable room light rather than bringing the phone extremely close solely for brightness. Nikon’s lens guide explains the relationship between subject distance and perspective. The illustration shows a simulated viewpoint comparison, not a measured optical test or a GlowPop export.
sections.detail-1.heading: What our camera provides
sections.detail-1.body: It combines a front-camera preview with adjustable screen color and brightness. The first five photos are free; Pro unlocks unlimited photos and video recording. No lens switching, face reshaping or automatic perspective repair is promised. Keep the phone at a comfortable distance and judge the actual saved photo, because camera processing and ambient light also affect its appearance.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: Will cropping a close selfie change its perspective?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: Cropping changes the framing. Move the camera first if you want a different relationship between near and far features.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: What if my face gets darker when the phone moves back?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: Try soft room light. It can help keep your face readable without forcing you to hold the phone very close again.

related.related.label: Use Screen Fill Light for Selfies in a Dim Room
steps.step-1.text: Start with a comfortable amount of room light. In GlowPop: Selfie Glow Camera, use the front-camera preview with a neutral screen-light color.
steps.step-2.text: Keep your head angle steady and move the phone modestly farther away. Reframe with your position, then adjust available brightness while checking comfort and facial highlights.
steps.step-3.text: Take a test photo and inspect the saved result. Compare framing and light separately. Keep whichever viewpoint suits your purpose, without treating one image as a verdict on how you look.
